Stochastic Matrix Class

Source: R/01_classes.R
StochMat.Rd

Construct and validate a square matrix of finite, nonnegative transition probabilities. The returned object has S3 class "StochMat".

Usage

new_StochMat(x, ...)

validate_StochMat(x, tol = 1e-12)

StochMat(...)

is.StochMat(x)

# S3 method for class 'StochMat'
print(x, digits = getOption("digits"), ...)

Arguments

x

For new_StochMat(), a matrix or data for base::matrix(). For is.StochMat(), the object to check. For validation or printing, a StochMat.

...

For the constructors, data and arguments for base::matrix() when the input is supplied as data rather than as a matrix. For the print method, additional arguments passed to base::print().

tol

Nonnegative numeric tolerance for the absolute difference between each row sum and one after clipping. The validator defaults to 1e-12.

digits

Number of significant digits used to round displayed values. Defaults to getOption("digits").

Value

The constructors and validator return a matrix of class "StochMat". is.StochMat() returns a single logical value. The print method invisibly returns the validated matrix.

Details

Input entries below -1e-16 are rejected. Entries in [-1e-16, 0) are set to zero. After clipping, each row sum must differ from one by at most 1e-12. A larger deviation is an error. Each accepted row is divided by its sum. StochMat() warns only if it clips negative entries.

Validation

A valid StochMat must satisfy all of:

  • is a square matrix (nrow(x) == ncol(x))

  • has at least one state

  • all entries are finite and nonnegative

  • every row sum is within 1e-12 of one

  • state names are unique, non-missing, and non-empty

Assign the returned object to retain corrections. is.StochMat() only checks validity.

See also

new_StochMat(), validate_StochMat(), is.StochMat()

Examples

StochMat(diag(3))
#> Stochastic Matrix
#>   dim: 3 x 3 
#>     1 2 3
#>   1 1 0 0
#>   2 0 1 0
#>   3 0 0 1
StochMat(matrix(c(0.2,0.8, 0.7,0.3), ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))
#> Stochastic Matrix
#>   dim: 2 x 2 
#>       1   2
#>   1 0.2 0.8
#>   2 0.7 0.3

m <- StochMat(diag(2))
is.StochMat(m)
#> [1] TRUE
